basis: Congenital structural or functional nervous system abnormalities; other organs are not consistently affected across this umbrella.
ATG16L1-associated immune-mediated intestinal inflammation; extraintestinal damage is not consistently present in at least 30%.
Chronic localized inflammatory skin disease with immune-mediated cutaneous vasculitis; no common extracutaneous organ damage.
Pregnancy-associated hepatic bile transport dysfunction; pruritus does not establish skin damage, and fetal complications are not maternal organ involvement.
Immune-mediated ulcerative inflammation involving the entire colon; no additional organ damage consistently meets the threshold.
Inherited glutamine metabolism disorder defined by neurologic dysfunction causing spasticity, ataxia and dysarthria.
RPE65-related retinal degeneration causes rod-cone dysfunction and visual loss; no established systemic involvement.
Carcinoma of the endocrine pancreas; metastatic sites and exocrine pancreatic dysfunction are not defining involvement.
Bone marrow hypoplasia and congenital neurologic abnormalities, including callosal agenesis and hydrocephalus, define the syndrome.
Placental trophoblastic disease lies outside the axes; vomiting is a symptom, and hyperthyroidism is not common direct thyroid damage.
Isolated reduced skeletal growth defines the phenotype; an endocrine or metabolic cause is not established.
Endometrial tissue within uterine myometrium affects a reproductive organ; bleeding does not establish intrinsic hematologic disease.
Congenital intestinal malrotation with midgut volvulus defines gastrointestinal involvement; facial dysmorphism alone adds no organ axis.
Trauma-associated ischemic bone necrosis; local interruption of blood supply does not establish a separate vascular disorder.
Developmental delay, hearing loss and VSD occur in 80-99%; Duane anomaly in 80-99% impairs eye movement. Urinary reflux (30-79%) omitted by cap.
Ocular malformations and neurodevelopmental abnormalities define the syndrome; pituitary hypoplasia (5/5) and hormone deficiencies support common endocrine dysfunction.
Acute malignant myeloid proliferation in blood and marrow; no additional organ damage established as common for this cytogenetic subtype.
Smooth muscle malignancy arising in the breast; breast is outside the axes, and histology does not establish locomotor muscle involvement.
Folate deficiency is a nutritional metabolic disturbance causing impaired hematopoiesis and megaloblastic anemia; no common additional organ damage.
Structural displacement of the stomach through the diaphragmatic hiatus; no common direct pulmonary or muscle damage.
Combined immunodeficiency with characteristic lymphopenia and neutropenia; recurrent infections do not establish lasting urinary or respiratory damage.
Congenital absence or underdevelopment of the humerus, often with associated forearm and joint malformations.
Malignancy of the uterine broad ligament affects reproductive supporting tissue, outside the locomotor connective tissue axis despite the parent classification.
Childhood chorea, developmental delay and intellectual disability establish a neurologic disorder; involuntary movement does not imply muscle disease.
Inherited rod-cone retinal degeneration with night blindness and visual impairment; no established extraocular involvement.
